items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: Minton is mentioned as the location of a gig ('this Minton's gig'), not as a person the interviewee interacted with personally.

ctx.x: Yup. And they’re good records. The first one was done — not the very first one, the first one was at an Army camp in New Jersey with Milt and I forget who the drummer was, and Tony. We played jobs all over. But when you got this Minton’s gig, it was about now, the early part of 1953, we were there about six months almost, it was really a fantastic gig, and the group got really tight. It was with Philly Joe and Milt and this was before — just between the time Milt went in, was with Cab Calloway and the time that…
Was it out of the ordinary for this — this was an integrated group at the time — was it out of the ordinary?
